headline: Jake LaRavia recorded a double-double on Monday with 15 points (6-of-10 FGs), 10 rebounds, one assist, two steals and one three-pointer against the Jazz.
body: LaRavia returned to the starting lineup after two games as a reserve. He took advantage of the opportunity by setting a new season high for scoring and recording his first double-double of the season. LaRavia’s scoring is down from last season, but he has been a decent source of steals. However, that isn’t enough for him to be considered a must-roster player, even if this was a strong performance.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Quentin Grimes contributed nine points (1-of-8 FGs), three rebounds, eight assists, one block and one three-pointer against the Jazz on Monday.
body: Grimes struggled with his shot in what could be his final start before Austin Reaves (heel) returns to the lineup, but he made up for it with his passing. He surpassed his season high of seven assists, which he set in his previous outing. In the three games since he scored 47 points, Grimes has scored a total of 42 points. It was a fun stretch for him as a starter, and if he gets the chance again, he’ll be worth streaming. However, initial reports had Reaves returning for either this game against Utah or for Friday’s game against the Spurs, so Grimes will likely return to a bench role in their next game.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Luka Dončić led the Lakers with 28 points (8-of-24 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, one steal and three three-pointers in a 109-94 win over the Jazz on Monday.
body: Dončić didn’t have his best shooting night, but he did enough to lead the Lakers in scoring and to a second straight win. They were also able to get some revenge after Utah ended their nine-game win streak last week. Dončić is still putting up strong numbers, but he has cooled off a bit after his scorching hot start to the season. They’ll take on the Spurs on Friday in what will be a battle for first place in the West.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Ace Bailey posted a full line on Monday with 18 points (8-of-16 FGs), five rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Lakers.
body: Bailey continues to provide well-rounded value in his second season, and he has shown tremendous growth. He did a little bit of everything in this game, though it wasn’t enough for Utah to get the win. Bailey will continue to be a solid producer with Lauri Markkanen (wrist) still sidelined for a while longer. He hasn’t had many big games, but he has been consistent.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Kyle Filipowski provided a boost off the bench with 21 points (8-of-14 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), 12 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in a 109-94 loss to the Lakers on Monday.
body: Filipowski wasn’t in the rotation to start the season despite Jusuf Nurkić being sidelined, which was concerning. However, he was able to take advantage of his opportunity in this game. He set season highs for points, rebounds and assists while recording his first double-double of the season. It took Nurkić and Jaxson Hayes being out for him to get minutes, so this doesn’t make him a must-add, though he’s worth keeping an eye on to see how he fits into the rotation moving forward.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Mo Bamba started on Monday and contributed six points (3-of-7 FGs), seven rebounds, two assists and two blocks against the Lakers.
body: Bamba got the starting nod with Jaxson Hayes (knee) sidelined for this game. However, he wasn’t able to replicate his production from his last few games as a starter. He played 29 minutes, but he was thoroughly outplayed by Kyle Filipowski, who played less than 24 minutes off the bench. It seems Bamba’s strong stretch as a starter wasn’t actually going to lead to him being a fantasy stud for the rest of the season. Who knew?
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Zach LaVine recorded 18 points (8-of-17 FGs), six rebounds, two assists, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Spurs.
body: On a night when backcourt partner Darius Acuff Jr. (12 points, one rebound and four assists) went 5-of-14 from the field, LaVine shot a solid percentage and scored 18 points. Since going off for 31 points in a November 10 loss to the Magic, the veteran guard has scored 19 points or less in five straight games. However, LaVine’s fantasy value remains strong, as he’s exceeded his ADP (103) by a few rounds in nine-cat formats.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Andre Hunter amassed 15 points (7-of-12 FGs), seven rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Spurs.
body: After dishing out eight assists total in his prior three appearances, Hunter matched that number on Monday. Those eight assists were double his previous high this season, and Hunter was also valuable to fantasy managers as a scorer and rebounder. However, as has been the case for most of his NBA career, Hunter’s inability to provide defensive stats keeps his fantasy value low.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keegan Murray accounted for 14 points (6-of-12 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Spurs.
body: After grabbing at least seven rebounds in three straight games, Murray recorded just two on Monday. Given Sacramento’s offense, he has to do more in areas outside of scoring to provide reliable fantasy value. That hasn’t happened consistently enough, which is why Murray’s fantasy value sits well outside the top-100 in nine-cat formats.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Domantas Sabonis finished Monday’s loss to the Spurs with 20 points (8-of-9 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), 12 rebounds and eight assists.
body: Despite foul trouble, Sabonis had one of his most productive nights of the season on Monday. The Kings center finished two assists shy of a triple-double and recorded his fourth 20-point game of the season. While establishing chemistry with rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. has been a struggle at times, Sabonis remains a valuable center in fantasy basketball, regardless of league format. The Kings play two more games in Week 6, starting with the Warriors on Wednesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brandon Miller (knee) is available to play against the Grizzlies on Monday.
body: As expected, Miller has officially been cleared to play after initially being listed as probable. He briefly exited from Friday’s game against the Hawks, but he was able to return to finish that game and will continue to suit up against Memphis.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Duncan Robinson (quad) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Magic.
body: Robinson should be re-evaluated sometime this week, but he will not play on Tuesday. Kevin Huerter has moved into the starting lineup and should remain there until Robinson is available.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Duren (hamstring) has been ruled out against the Magic on Tuesday.
body: Duren was set to be re-evaluated on Sunday, and while there hasn’t been another update to his status, he won’t return against Orlando. Hopefully they provide a new timeline for him soon, but it looks like John Collins will get another start at center, with Paul Reed filling out the backup minutes down low.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Cade Cunningham (knee) is probable for Tuesday’s game against the Magic.
body: Cunningham’s right knee has been an issue for a little while now, but he’s only missed one game. The probable tag suggests that he’ll be available on Tuesday. If not, Daniss Jenkins’ role would likely expand.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Paul George (rest) is not on the injury report for Tuesday’s game against the Wizards.
body: George will be back after getting a rest night on the second leg of Boston’s back-to-back on Sunday. Jayson Tatum got the night off on Saturday, which allowed Sam Hauser to start both games. Hauser will head back to the bench against Washington.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Mitchell Robinson (illness) has been ruled out against the Wizards on Tuesday.
body: This will be a third straight absence for Robinson. Neemias Queta should continue to take on a few extra minutes at center, with Luka Garza filling out the backup minutes down low.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jaxson Hayes (knee) has been ruled out against the Lakers on Monday.
body: Hayes exited early on Sunday and will be held out for the second leg of Utah’s back-to-back. Mo Bamba, who had been on fire with Hayes out previously, should return to the starting lineup.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Ryan Dunn (quad) is available for Monday’s matchup with the Pelicans.
body: Dunn made an early exit Friday against the Jazz, but he’s in good shape following a weekend of rest. Dunn should continue to see his usual allotment of minutes off the bench.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Bryce McGowens (elbow) is available for Monday’s matchup with the Suns.
body: McGowens is back in action following a five-game absence, but his availability isn’t particularly meaningful to fantasy hoops managers given his limited role in New Orleans’ rotation.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Alex Caruso (hip) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Pacers.
body: Caruso joins a number of Thunder players on an extensive injury report, including Nikola Topic (hip) which means OKC will have to get creative with its lineups. Guys like Bennett Stirtz, Nique Clifford and Josh Dix could all see additional minutes.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Brandin Podziemski recorded a team-high 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds and two assists over 37 minutes to lead the Warriors to an 88-87 win over the Celtics on Sunday.
body: Podziemski helped Golden State snap a five-game losing streak in a low-scoring slugfest where both teams shot below 40 percent from the floor and failed to reach 90 points. He knocked down a clutch three-pointer to put the Warriors ahead with just over two minutes left on the clock and they managed to hold off the Celtics the rest of the way. He’ll continue to play an increased role while Stephen Curry remains sidelined with a partially-torn oblique. The Warriors have a three-game week on tap that includes matchups against the Kings, Trail Blazers and Clippers.
author: George Bissell

headline: Jayson Tatum amassed 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, six assists and one steal over 38 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: Tatum scored 23 first-half points to pass Bill Russell for eighth place on the franchise’s all-time scoring list and keep Boston within striking distance. It wasn’t enough as he went ice-cold in the second half as the Celtics dropped their fourth straight game. He missed a critical free throw in the final minute before failing to nail a wide-open three-pointer that would’ve put the Celtics ahead in the final 30 seconds. He had a chance to deliver a game-winner following a huge steal by Hugo González, but missed a fadeaway over Draymond Green. The 28-year-old fantasy star has delivered second-round value this season, averaging 26.4 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.7 assists, 0.7 steals and 0.7 blocks through 15 games. The Celtics have a three-game week coming up featuring showdowns against the Wizards, Hawks and Spurs.
author: George Bissell

headline: Charles Bassey chipped in 13 points (6-of-7 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists and three steals over 26 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Celtics.
body: Bassey delivered double-digit points for the third consecutive start shortly after Warriors head coach Steve Kerr told reporters that he wants to give Bassey an extended opportunity at center with Draymond Green moving to power forward. The decision paid dividends as Bassey came within one board of his second straight double-double. The well-traveled 26-year-old big man has looked like a viable fantasy option recently and is a worthwhile pickup in deeper formats. The Warriors have a three-game week coming up that includes matchups against the Kings, Trail Blazers and Clippers.
author: George Bissell

headline: Derrick White notched 14 points (6-of-21 FGs), three rebounds, five assists and one steal over 31 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: White was held scoreless in the opening half, but knocked down a couple clutch buckets in the final five minutes of regulation. He was open a couple times in the final minute but passed on those looks to feed Jayson Tatum, who missed a pair of potential go-ahead shots. He finished just 2-of-12 from three-point range and is shooting below 30 percent for the season from that range. The Celtics struggled to find secondary scoring to complement Tatum with Paul George sitting out for load management reasons on the second night of a back-to-back. The Celtics have a three-game week coming up featuring showdowns against the Wizards, Hawks and Spurs.
author: George Bissell

headline: Ivica Zubac tallied 10 points (5-of-11 FGs), 14 rebounds and one assist in Sunday’s loss to the Knicks.
body: Zubac recorded his sixth double-double of the season on Sunday, but unfortunately, there were no defensive stats to speak of. Entering the season with a fifth-round ADP, the 7-footer’s production has underwhelmed, and he ranks outside the top-100 in nine-cat formats. Of course, Tyrese Haliburton’s hamstring injury hasn’t helped, and many of Zubac’s other Pacers teammates have been affected as well, to no one’s surprise. Getting Haliburton back, which could happen by the end of November, would be huge for all the Pacers, including Zubac.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Andrew Nembhard recorded 16 points (5-of-13 FGs, 4-of-7 FTs), two rebounds, eight assists and two three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Knicks.
body: Nembhard led the way for the Pacers with eight assists, but he also committed six turnovers. While Braden Smith (6/1/4) gave the Pacers solid minutes off the bench, the absence of Tyrese Haliburton or T.J. McConnell to play off of tends to hurt Nembhard’s efficiency. Sitting just outside the top-100 in nine-cat formats, Nembhard’s current production aligns with his preseason ADP (117).
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kelly Oubre Jr. amassed 15 points (4-of-10 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs) and five rebounds in Sunday’s loss to the Knicks.
body: Oubre’s ability to get to the foul line gave his point total a welcome boost, but his overall production was underwhelming. Over the last two weeks, the Pacers’ wing has been a top-100 player, but the season-long value remains relatively low. The Pacers play three games in Week 6, starting with the Thunder on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Pascal Siakam finished Sunday’s loss to the Knicks with 25 points (9-of-22 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals and three three-pointers.
body: While he didn’t shoot a high percentage, Siakam extended his streak of games with at least 20 points to four on Sunday. In fact, he last scored fewer than 19 points on November 1. While Tyrese Haliburton’s hamstring injury has changed the equation for the entire Pacers’ rotation, Siakam’s fantasy value has held steady. Given what happened last season, most fantasy managers will take that.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Josh Hart finished Sunday’s win over the Pacers with 10 points (5-of-11 FGs), 11 rebounds, 10 assists and one steal.
body: Having struggled for much of the season’s first month, Hart needed a night like Sunday. It was a historic one: he recorded his 18th triple-double for the Knicks. That moved him into a tie for second place on the franchise’s all-time list with the late Michael Ray Richardson, and Hart trails Walt Frazier by five for the top spot. Even if the shots aren’t falling, Hart can provide solid fantasy value, which is why he’s still rostered in 79 percent of Yahoo leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Landry Shamet amassed 17 points (7-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.
body: Back in the Knicks’ starting lineup for a second straight night, Shamet had another productive outing. He’s made at least two three-pointers in five straight games, and the veteran guard has provided reliable late-round fantasy value over the last two weeks. Rostered in 15 percent of Yahoo leagues, Shamet is worth streaming as long as OG Anunoby (calf) is out.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Anthony Black accumulated 14 points (5-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Wizards.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Franz Wagner tallied 16 points (7-of-18 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists and two steals in Sunday’s loss to the Wizards.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Desmond Bane finished Sunday’s loss to the Wizards with 17 points (7-of-14 FGs), one rebound, five assists, one steal and three three-pointers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: AJ Dybantsa produced 16 points (4-of-10 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists and one steal in Sunday’s win over the Magic.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Trae Young tallied 11 points (3-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, 11 assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Magic.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kyshawn George amassed 24 points (9-of-17 FGs), three rebounds, four assists, one block and six three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Magic.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Anthony Davis notched 22 points (8-of-13 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Magic.
body: Davis has scored at least 22 points in four straight games as he continues to exceed preseason expectations. However, AD beginning the season with an ADP in the 40s had nothing to do with production; it was all about availability. Knock on wood, but he’s been available for 16 of the Wizards’ first 18 games. If that continues, Davis managers should be in a great spot. The Wizards play two games in Week 6, starting with the Celtics on Tuesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Bam Adebayo recorded a triple-double with 24 points (8-of-11 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), 15 rebounds, 12 assists, two steals and three blocks over 37 minutes, leading the Heat to a 123-113 win over the Thunder on Sunday.
body: This marquee matchup lost some of its luster with generational talents Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin) and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (back, neck) both sidelined by injuries. Adebayo picked up the scoring slack with an exceptionally efficient performance, recording his ninth career triple-double, accomplishing the feat for the first time since November 29, 2024. The most impressive part of this effort was that he reached the 20-point plateau on just 11 shot attempts while earning only nine trips to the free-throw line. The Heat have a challenging three-game week ahead featuring road matchups against fellow Eastern Conference contenders in the 76ers, Knicks and Cavaliers.
author: George Bissell

headline: Jared McCain posted a team-high 20 points (7-of-17 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), two rebounds and three assists over 29 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Heat.
body: Oklahoma City leaned on both McCain and backcourt mate Ajay Mitchell to carry their offense with perennial MVP candidate Shai Gilgeous-Alexander sitting this one out, likely for precautionary reasons, due to back and neck issues. McCain matched a season-high with 17 field goal attempts and has scored at least 18 points in seven of his last nine games since November 6. He’s still a one-dimensional scoring threat for fantasy purposes, but his increased role with the Thunder should keep him on fantasy radar screens. The Thunder have a quick turnaround with a road tilt against the Pacers on Monday before facing the Timberwolves and Bucks to close out a three-game week.
author: George Bissell

headline: Bennett Stirtz scored a season-high 21 points (7-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds and five assists over 32 minutes off the bench in Sunday’s loss to the Heat.
body: Stirtz predictably saw increased opportunities off the bench spelling both Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain with superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander sitting out with back and neck issues. He established season-high marks in points (21), minutes (32) and shot attempts (14) while also dishing out five assists. The unheralded 23-year-old is rapidly becoming a key contributor for the injury-ravaged Thunder, averaging 15 points over his last three games. The Thunder have a quick turnaround with a road tilt against the Pacers on Monday before facing the Timberwolves and Bucks to close out a three-game week.
author: George Bissell

headline: Ajay Mitchell supplied 17 points (6-of-17 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and two steals over 22 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Heat.
body: Mitchell became one of the focal points for Oklahoma City with primary catalyst Shai Gilgeous-Alexander sidelined with neck and back issues. The 24-year-old guard has played a much larger role this season for the injury-depleted Thunder than previously envisioned, averaging a career-high 28 minutes through 15 games. He’s cooled down considerably after a sizzling-hot start to the year and hasn’t reached 20 points in any of his last six games since early November. The Thunder are back in action with a road matchup against the Pacers on Monday before closing out a three-game week against the Timberwolves and Bucks.
author: George Bissell

headline: Victor Wembanyama (back) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Kings.
body: Wembanyama, who torched the Pelicans on Saturday, is dealing with lower back tightness. If he can’t play against the Kings, Luke Kornet is the most likely replacement in the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jordan McLaughlin (shoulder) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Kings.
body: McLaughlin is dealing with a left shoulder contusion. Under normal circumstances, his availability would not affect fantasy basketball. However, with De’Aaron Fox (shin) also questionable, McLaughlin could play more if he’s available.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Aaron Fox (shin) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Kings.
body: Fox is on the injury report due to a left shin contusion. With Dylan Harper (hip) already out, the Spurs could be down two perimeter starters on Monday. If Fox can’t play, Harrison Barnes could move into the starting lineup, and the Spurs may also have to give Jordan McLaughlin more minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Derrick White, Hugo González, Jayson Tatum, Sam Hauser and Neemias Queta will start Sunday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Tatum is back after sitting out Saturday’s loss to the Kings, but Paul George is out. As a result, Hauser will start again. The other change is White, whose return means that Payton Pritchard will come off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaxson Hayes (knee) will not return to Sunday’s game against the Mavericks.
body: Hayes’ night is finished after playing 12 minutes in the first half of Sunday’s game. The knee is the same one that cost him two games earlier this month; hopefully, this won’t be a long-term issue. With Hayes done for the night, the Jazz will rely on Mo Bamba, with Tony Bradley moving into the backup role.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaylon Tyson (ankle) is probable for Monday’s game against the Bulls.
body: Tyson is on track to return after missing the Cavaliers’ last three games with a right ankle injury. His return could reduce Sam Merrill’s playing time, as he logged 25 minutes in Friday’s win over the Pacers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ousmane Dieng (finger) is questionable to play against the Raptors on Monday.
body: Dieng underwent surgery on his finger a week prior to this, but there is a chance he is back against Toronto. Dieng’s role has been small this season, so his return won’t have much of an impact on the rotation.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (back, neck) is out for Sunday’s game against the Heat.
body: Initially listed as questionable, Gilgeous-Alexander will sit out Sunday’s game with back and neck injuries. Bennett Stirtz’s role may increase, with the rookie potentially making his first NBA start out of necessity.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Clint Capela (ankle) is not on the injury report for Monday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Capela will be back after missing three weeks due to this ankle injury. He’ll fill out some of the backup center minutes alongside Steven Adams, which won’t be enough time for him to impact much in fantasy basketball.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Grant Nelson (ankle) is probable for Monday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Nelson is on track to be available for Monday’s game, which would be his first action of the NBA season if he were to play. His availability doesn’t affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Collin Murray-Boyles (concussion) is probable to play against the Bucks on Monday.
body: CMB participated in practice on Sunday and is now expected to return from a one-game absence against Milwaukee. Allen Graves filled in as a starter on Friday and was able to have a productive night, but he’ll return to the bench with CMB expected back.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Trey Murphy (knee) is probable to play against the Suns on Monday.
body: Murphy missed Saturday’s game against the Spurs, which was the second night of a back-to-back following his return from a a six-game absence. He came off the bench in his last appearance, though if he returns to the starting unit, Saddiq Bey or Herbert Jones will return to the bench.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Trendon Watford (ankle) is out for Monday’s game against the Suns.
body: Monday’s game will be the ninth Watford has missed due to a sprained right ankle. His continued absence does not affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Bryce McGowens (elbow) is probable for Monday’s game against the Suns.
body: McGowens is on track to return after missing five games due to a right elbow infection. His return could push Jaron Pierre out of the rotation, but neither player has been an impactful fantasy option.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Norman Powell has been diagnosed with a right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated later this week.
body: Powell was initially listed as questionable to play on Sunday but is now officially out. This likely also means he will miss the Bulls’ games on Monday and Wednesday as well, which will open up a starting spot. Patrick Williams and Buddy Hield should both see expanded roles, with one of them likely to start.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Darius Acuff Jr. tallied a team-high 21 points (7-of-23 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds and eight assists over 40 minutes to lead the Kings to a 97-96 win over the Celtics.
body: Acuff has an extremely bright future as a dynamic, high-volume scoring machine and he’s starting to become more efficient as his rookie season progresses. He continues to have a permanent green light to attack on the offensive end of the floor and he had little trouble slashing and creating shots against some of Boston’s stronger defenders in this one. He’s still prone to the occasional defensive lapse, but that figures to get cleaned up over time. The 20-year-old lottery pick is averaging 25.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 0.9 steals through 16 games. He’s clearly on the ascent as a fantasy contributor and looks like a potential franchise cornerstone for Sacramento to build around. They’re just 2-14 this season and have a three-game slate coming up with matchups against the Spurs, Warriors and Timberwolves.
author: George Bissell

headline: Mike Conley delivered a team-high 19 points (6-of-7 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and three steals off the bench in Saturday’s loss to the Kings.
body: Things unraveled in the third quarter as Boston went 0-for-15 from three-point range and were outscored 35-13 in the frame. Conley was one of the few bright spots in this one, coming off the bench to help lead a late comeback effort that fell just short. The 39-year-old veteran saw a huge spike in minutes with Derrick White (shoulder) sitting out and Payton Pritchard struggling to get going offensively. He was a perfect 4-of-4 from three-point range and also added three steals. He’s a non-factor for fantasy purposes at this stage of his career, but he could wind up playing an important role for Boston as a steadying presence in the postseason. The Celtics have lost three straight and will close out the week with a road tilt against the Stephen Curry-less Warriors on Sunday.
author: George Bissell

headline: Domantas Sabonis amassed 15 points (5-of-10 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), 17 rebounds, four assists and one block over 32 minutes in Saturday’s win over the Celtics.
body: Sabonis took a backseat on the offensive end of the floor with rookie Darius Acuff Jr. doing most of the driving for Sacramento, but he was a real factor on the glass, especially in the second half when Boston’s starting center Neemias Queta was forced to the bench with foul trouble. The fact that Jayson Tatum, an outstanding rebounder in his own right, sat this one out for load management reasons also helped. He committed seven turnovers, but it didn’t end up mattering as the Kings got hot in the third quarter and managed to pick up their second win of the year. Sabonis is averaging 14.1 points, 13.6 rebounds and 5.3 assists through 15 games this season. The Kings have a three-game slate coming up with matchups against the Spurs, Warriors and Timberwolves.
author: George Bissell

headline: Paul George posted 19 points (6-of-21 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), eight rebounds, five assists, four steals and one block over 37 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Kings.
body: George finished just 2-of-9 from three-point range as the Celtics shot an abysmal 22 percent (13-of-58) from long range with both Jayson Tatum (rest) and Derrick White (shoulder) sitting this one out. They built a 13-point lead by halftime, but went ice-cold in the third quarter, which allowed Sacramento to get back into the game. George has arguably been Boston’s most reliable all-around contributor this season, averaging 19.9 points, 5.6 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 2.2 steals through 14 games. The Celtics have lost three straight and will close out the week with a road tilt against the Stephen Curry-less Warriors on Sunday.
author: George Bissell

headline: De’Andre Hunter chipped in 20 points (5-of-11 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), six rebounds, two assists and one block over 41 minutes in Saturday’s win over the Celtics.
body: Hunter has always seemed to have Boston’s number and managed to get to the free-throw line nearly 10 times in this one while also hitting 2-of-5 from three-point range. He’s been a curious fit with Sacramento, his third team in the last three seasons, but he’s still capable of scoring in bunches and supplying a couple boards and assists on a consistent basis. He’s a viable streaming option in deeper fantasy leagues at this stage of his career. The Kings have a three-game slate coming up with matchups against the Spurs, Warriors and Timberwolves.
author: George Bissell

headline: Cam Spencer amassed nine points (4-of-8 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, six assists and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
body: While Ty Jerome’s return from a hip injury meant Spencer resumed his usual backup duties, his playing time was unaffected. With Javon Small (personal) away from the team, Spencer still played 30 minutes and provided solid value in assists. Rostered in 47 percent of Yahoo leagues, the third-year guard has been close to a top-100 player in nine-cat formats. He’s worth holding onto, even with Jerome’s return.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jahmai Mashack recorded zero points (0-of-1 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block in Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
body: Mashack wasn’t on the fantasy radar before Saturday’s game, and his lack of production certainly didn’t change that. He started for Cameron Boozer, who was sidelined with a sprained right ankle, and played 22 minutes. Mashack could get another start against the Hornets on Monday if Boozer remains out, but there’s no need to consider rostering him in redraft leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cedric Coward finished Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 23 points (8-of-16 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals and four three-pointers.
body: Coward led the Grizzlies in scoring on Saturday, shooting 50 percent from the field. However, he also committed a game-high six turnovers, the most he’s had in an NBA game. In addition to his points, the rebounds, steals and three-pointers should help offset the high turnover count for fantasy managers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ty Jerome (hip) tallied 18 points (7-of-17 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
body: Back in the Grizzlies’ lineup after a four-game absence, Jerome showed some signs of rust on Saturday. However, to say that was the lone reason for his five-turnover night would be unfair to the Timberwolves, who have one of the best collections of perimeter defenders in the NBA. This wasn’t Jerome’s best night, but his ability to play 27 minutes without aggravating the hip injury is a positive going into Week 6. Memphis plays four games next week, starting with the Hornets on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: LaMelo Ball notched 12 points (5-of-10 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Saturday’s win over the Grizzlies.
body: With Jaden McDaniels, Ayo Dosunmu and Jonathan Kuminga (16/4/2 with one block and two three-pointers) all scoring at least 16 points, Ball took a step back scoring-wise on Saturday. After an inefficient shooting night against the Knicks on Thursday, the Timberwolves’ point guard made 50 percent of his attempts against the Grizzlies. Even better for fantasy managers was that Ball recorded a full stat line, his second of the season and the first since a November 4 win over the Rockets. Minnesota plays four games next week, starting with the Nets on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaden McDaniels accounted for 25 points (11-of-17 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s win over the Grizzlies.
body: A double-digit scorer in all 17 games he’s played this season, McDaniels scored a season-high 25 points on Saturday. The Timberwolves forward, already one of the NBA’s top on-ball defenders, is enjoying his most productive offensive season. McDaniels is averaging career highs in points, rebounds, assists and three-pointers. Given the ADP of 85, he may be one of the early steals of the season in fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ayo Dosunmu recorded 19 points (9-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, two assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Saturday’s win over the Grizzlies.
body: After scoring at least 18 points in each of Minnesota’s first six games of November, Dosunmu has run “hot and cold” recently. Limited to six points in Thursday’s loss to the Knicks, he rebounded nicely on Saturday. Even with the recent run of inconsistent scoring, Dosunmu has been a top-50 fantasy player over the last month. With Anthony Edwards (knee) not having a return timeline, Dosunmu is well-positioned to provide reliable fantasy value for the foreseeable future.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kyrie Irving amassed 25 points (8-of-24 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), six rebounds and four assists over 35 minutes to lift the Mavericks to a 110-100 victory over the Clippers.
body: Irving got off to a sluggish start by his lofty standards but he responded with a 16-point performance in the second half to help Dallas pull away for good. The 34-year-old point guard hasn’t skipped a beat in his return from last year’s knee surgery, averaging 22.5 points, 3.8 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.2 steals through 13 games this season. The Mavericks close out the week with a road tilt against the Jazz on Sunday.
author: George Bissell

headline: Brook Lopez delivered a team-high 21 points (8-of-15 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), six rebounds and one block over 25 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Mavericks.
body: Lopez has been an unexpected impact fantasy contributor during his age-38 campaign, scoring 20 points or more in three consecutive games and six of his last eight overall since November 4. He’s taken advantage of his opportunity to play a larger role on the rebuilding Clippers following their turbulent offseason and figures to be on the move to a contender at the upcoming trade deadline. He should be rostered in all fantasy leagues at this juncture. The Clippers have a busy four-game week upcoming with showdowns against the Rockets, Grizzlies, Pelicans and Warriors on tap.
author: George Bissell

headline: Precious Achiuwa (leg) is available for Saturday’s game against the Celtics.
body: Achiuwa is back after sitting out Friday’s loss to the Lakers. His return may mean Keegan Murray doesn’t have to play as much as he did on Friday, when he logged 39 minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jeremiah Fears, Herb Jones, Saddiq Bey, Derik Queen and Yves Missi will start Saturday’s game against the Spurs.
body: The Pelicans are without Trey Murphy and Zion Williamson for Saturday’s game. They’ve been replaced in the lineup by Bey and Queen, and both should already be rostered in 12-team leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kyrie Irving, Cooper Flagg, Caleb Martin, Zaccharie Risacher and Daniel Gafford will start Saturday’s game against the Clippers.
body: The Mavericks are without P.J. Washington for Saturday’s game due to a shoulder injury. Risacher will get the start, but Naji Marshall should also see more playing time.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ty Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Jahmai Mashack and Zach Edey will start Saturday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Jerome is back after a four-game absence, and his return pushes Cam Spencer to the bench. The other change is Mashack, who makes his first start of the season in place of the injured Cameron Boozer.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Zion Williamson (thigh) is out for Saturday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Absent from the Pelicans’ initial injury report, Williamson won’t play on Saturday due to a left thigh contusion. With Trey Murphy (knee) also out, the Pelicans will have to lean heavily on Saddiq Bey and Jeremiah Fears for scoring. Also, look for Jordan Poole to take on a larger role.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Damian Lillard, Sidy Cissoko, Toumani Camara, Deni Avdija and Donovan Clingan will start Saturday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Avdija is back after a two-game absence, and his return pushes Jayson Kent to the bench. That’s the only change to the Trail Blazers’ starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges, Landry Shamet, Josh Hart and Andre Drummond will start Saturday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: The Knicks are down two starters, as OG Anunoby (calf) and Karl-Anthony Towns (illness) are out. Shamet and Drummond are moving into the starting lineup, and both are worth streaming.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Evans (illness) is available for Saturday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: Evans, added to the injury report early Saturday afternoon, is good to go. However, he hasn’t been in the rotation most nights, so the rookie’s availability won’t affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Walter Clayton Jr. (knee) is available for Saturday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Clayton is good to go after initially being questionable for Saturday’s game. As a result, Marcus Sasser will remain outside of the Mavericks’ rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: P.J. Washington (shoulder) is out for Saturday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Washington will miss a game for the first time this season, opening up a spot in the Mavericks’ starting lineup. Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher are potential replacements; both should play more, regardless of who head coach Dusty May slides into the lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Precious Achiuwa (leg) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Celtics.
body: Achiuwa did not play in Friday’s loss to the Lakers, and his absence contributed to Keegan Murray playing 39 minutes. Murray’s playing time may decrease if Achiuwa plays, but not by much.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Myles Turner recorded five points (1-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, one steal, four blocks and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kyle Kuzma tallied 12 points (4-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brayden Burries accounted for 26 points (12-of-20 FGs), eight rebounds, four assists, one block and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tyler Herro finished Saturday’s loss to the 76ers with 50 points (15-of-23 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), 11 rebounds, seven assists, one steal and seven three-pointers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Anfernee Simons amassed 18 points (6-of-13 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one assist and four three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Dominick Barlow accounted for 12 points (5-of-6 FGs), four rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer in Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Derrick White (shoulder) is out for Saturday’s game against the Kings.
body: White is out after initially being listed as questionable. Payton Pritchard, who usually comes off the bench, could move into the starting lineup, raising his fantasy ceiling.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jayson Tatum (rest) is out for Saturday’s game against the Kings.
body: Tatum is out after being listed as questionable on the Celtics’ initial injury report. With Boston visiting Golden State on Sunday, Tatum could play against the Warriors while Paul George gets that game off. As for the open spot in the starting lineup, Sam Hauser could be the replacement.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Mitchell Robinson (illness) is out for Saturday’s game against the Kings.
body: Robinson is out after not being listed on the Celtics’ initial injury report. Boston will rely mainly on Neemias Queta and Luka Garza at center, and rookie Chris Cenac Jr. could get rotation minutes after a strong showing in Wednesday’s loss to the Nuggets.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tyrese Maxey recorded 17 points (4-of-11 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), four rebounds, four assists and one block in Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Karl-Anthony Towns (illness) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Towns is a new addition to the Knicks’ injury report, and that’s generally not a good sign. If he can’t play, the Knicks will have to rely on Andre Drummond and James Wiseman to fill the void.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: OG Anunoby (calf) is now doubtful for Saturday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Initially questionable for Saturday’s game, Anunoby is trending toward not playing. If he can’t play, Landry Shamet will likely enter the starting lineup, with Josh Hart sliding down to power forward.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jabari Smith Jr. finished with 21 points (7-of-8 FGs), four rebounds, three assists and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Friday.
body: Following a hot start to the season, Smith has cooled down a bit in the month of November. This was his first time scoring at least 20 points in a game since Oct. 31, and he only did it because he was insanely efficient. Hopefully, his volume will start to tick back up so he can get back to being elite for fantasy managers, as he was in October. He’ll look to carry this production into their next matchup with the Clippers on Monday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Fred VanVleet lit up the Nuggets with 25 points (10-of-21 FGs), one rebound, nine assists, one steal and three three-pointers on Friday.
body: Despite missing all of last season, VanVleet has still been solid in fantasy basketball so far this year. He was able to set a new season high for scoring in this game, making this the first time he scored at least 25 points in a game since March of 2025. VanVleet’s presence in the lineup has been huge for Houston this year, and he proved in this game that he’s still capable of big scoring nights, even if they aren’t going to come consistently.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Luka Dončić put up 25 points (9-of-18 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, two steals, two 3-pointers, and six turnovers in the 106-104 win over the Kings.
body: Luka continues to dominate the game and the Kings couldn’t do much to stop him. In the clutch, Keegan Murray did get a steal on him which could’ve cost the Lakers the game. You would wish the turnover numbers go down, but with the load that he’s had to do on offense, it’s hard to complain too much. He’s dominating everyone else from a statistical basis that is helping you in other areas.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Alperen Şengün led the Rockets with 28 points (9-of-16 FGs, 9-of-13 FTs), 11 rebounds, 10 assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in a 133-124 loss to the Nuggets on Friday.
body: Şengün recorded his second triple-double of the season, but it wasn’t enough for Houston to secure the win. It has been a fantastic season for Şengün so far, as he is currently averaging career highs in points, assists, three-pointers and free throw percentage. He has been on the cusp of this type of production over the last few seasons, and it seems like he’s finally reaching it. The Rockets have started the season well, and Şengün has been right at the center of it.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Christian Braun lit up the Rockets with 19 points (7-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, four steals, one block and three three-pointers in a 133-124 win on Friday.
body: Last year was a down one for Braun, but he has bounced back to start this season. The offense is starting to pick up, but it’s his defensive impact that has been the biggest difference. He has at least one steal in every game this season and has had two or more in 10 of his 14 games, which has led to his career-high 2.3 steals per game. That’s carrying his category league value right now, which means he’s mostly been a one-trick pony, though he has been decent in a few other categories.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Quentin Grimes got himself 13 points (2-of-7 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists, and a three in the win over the Kings on Friday.
body: Grimes started off slowly but got going later in the game and helped the Lakers hold on. He’s still worth holding, but coach JJ Reddick did say that he’s hoping to have Austin Reaves back on Monday against the Jazz, or on Friday against the San Antonio Spurs. So sell high if you can, or ride it out and drop when Reaves comes back.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Cameron Johnson finished with 19 points (7-of-13 FGs), three rebounds, six assists, two steals and two three-pointers against the Rockets on Friday.
body: It has been another rough season in Denver for Johnson, but this was one of his best performances of the season, which included a new season high for assists. Johnson had a strong final season in Brooklyn, but he hasn’t been able to achieve that level of production during his two seasons as a Nugget. However, if he is able to provide lines like this, especially on a quieter night from Jamal Murray, Denver and fantasy managers will both be happy.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Walker Kessler put up 15 points (7-of-11 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, a steal, and three blocks, and a three in the win over the Kings.
body: Kessler had a very good game despite being in foul trouble. He had his way with Sabonis being in the paint and put up some good numbers. The two free throws he missed where in the clutch to ice the game. He hit a three in this game which was the first of the season. However, it’s a good performance all things considered.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: DeMar DeRozan provided a boost off the bench with 15 points (4-of-11 FGs), two rebounds, two assists and one steal against the Rockets on Friday.
body: DeRozan started this season scoring in double figures in each of Denver’s first three games. In the 10 games since, he has only scored in double figures three more times. The positive news is that he’s reached that mark in back-to-back games. DeRozan isn’t going to provide value anywhere near what he has throughout his career, but if he can continue to be a reliable bench scorer for Denver, he’ll be a valuable piece for this team when the playoffs arrive.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Domantas Sabonis got himself 19 points (8-of-13 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 16 rebounds, an assist and a three in the loss to the Lakers on Friday.
body: Sabonis continues to chug along and be efficient from the field. He did a good job on the offensive end and helping keep the Kings in the game, but he didn’t do a good job preventing Walker Kessler from having a good game. He at least got more shot attempts in this game after it’s been lackluster for the past few games.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Alperen Şengün (eye) will be available against the Nuggets on Friday.
body: Şengün sustained the injury against the Pacers in the second quarter and didn’t return. He should hopefully go back to producing at the level he was prior to the injury. He’s averaging 21.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, and 6.8 assists on the season.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Steven Adams (quad) is available to play against the Nuggets on Friday.
body: Adams was initially listed as questionable for this game, but he will be good to go. With Alperen Şengün available, Adams will fill out the backup center minutes.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Lakers head coach JJ Redick said the “hope” is that Austin Reaves (heel) will return in one of the Lakers’ next two games.
body: Following their matchup with the Kings on Friday, the Lakers will play the Jazz at home on Monday and the Spurs in San Antonio on Friday. It’s good to have some clarity on Reaves’ injury, but it also means Quentin Grimes’ time as a starter is likely coming to an end. If Reaves waits until Friday to play, Grimes should be streamed on Monday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Derrick White (shoulder) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Kings.
body: If White were to miss time, look for Payton Pritchard to be the main beneficiary of the absence. After that, it’s likely to be a lot of the Celtics role players getting marginal bumps.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Jayson Tatum (rest) is questionable to play against the Kings on Saturday.
body: Boston may be looking to give Tatum a night off against Sacramento before they play the Warriors on Saturday. If that’s the case, Sam Hauser will likely get the starting nod in place of Tatum.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: The Thunder will start Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain, Aday Mara, and Isaiah Hartenstein against the Pelicans on Friday.
body: It was previously reported that Micah Peavy would be starting in place Aday Mara, but Mara will get the nod. Mara is a streamer and Peavy isn’t anything more than a deeper league guy.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: The Raptors will start Immanuel Quickley, Ja’Kobe Walter, Scottie Barnes, Allen Graves, and Jakob Poeltl on Friday against the Pistons.
body: Collin Murray-Boyles will not play tonight and is replaced by rookie Allen Graves. Given Graves’s fantasy profile, if you want to stream him in, you might get a good performance.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Ron Holland (knee) has been ruled out against the Raptors on Friday.
body: For some reason, Detroit upgraded Holland to doubtful ahead of this game, and he has now officially been ruled out. This will be a third straight absence for him, which should allow Isaiah Joe and Chaz Lanier to continue taking on a few extra minutes.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: The Cavaliers will start James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Tyrese Proctor, Peyton Watson, and Jarrett Allen on Friday against the Pacers.
body: Peyton Watson returns to the starting lineup with Mario Hezonja heading back to the bench. For now, Watson is just a stream guy and Hezonja is only a deeper league type of player.
author: Brian Taylor Mario Hezonja

headline: Cade Cunningham (knee) is available to play against the Raptors on Friday.
body: As expected, Cunningham will return following a one-game absence. Javonte Green, who was excellent as a spot starter, will return to playing a role off the bench.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: The Nets will start Nolan Traoré, Danny Wolf, Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle, and Day’Ron Sharpe on Friday against Bulls.
body: The Nets will replace Egor in the starting lineup and replace him with Danny Wolf. This will be something to monitor going forward, but for now, Wolf could be used as a streamer and we’ll see how coach Jordi Fernandez distributes the minutes.
author: Brian Taylor Egor Dëmin

headline: Noa Essengue (wrist) will be available to play Friday against the Wizards.
body: Noa was listed as probable before this game, so it’s good to see that he’s giving it a go. Hopefully it doesn’t flare up and have him miss some time. Noa is just a deeper league guy, even with the Caleb Wilson injury.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: T.J. McConnell (hamstring) is available to play against the Cavaliers on Friday.
body: McConnell was initially listed as probable for this game, so his availability doesn’t come as a surprise. He continues to pop up on the injury report, but he hasn’t missed a game since he made his season debut two weeks ago. He may lose a few minutes with Andrew Nembhard back.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Peyton Watson (back) will be available to play against the Pacers on Friday.
body: He missed the past couple games with a back injury. With him coming back, it is possible that he returns to the starting lineup and causes Sam Merrill to come back to the bench. As of right now, he’s only a stream option for most redraft leagues.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Trey Murphy (knee) will play but with a minutes limit against the Thunder on Friday.
body: Murphy returns from a six game absence from a knee injury. With him returning, Saddiq Bey will likely head back to the bench and still be an option if you need points and three’s.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Alex Caruso (hip) will not play against the Pelicans on Friday.
body: He played nine minutes against the Hawks before leaving with a hip injury and didn’t return. Look for Bennett Stirtz and Nique Clifford to take more minutes in this game, but both of them are deeper league options and not streamers in most redraft leagues.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Jalen Smith (illness) has been ruled out against the Wizards on Friday.
body: Smith will be sidelined for this game after popping up on the injury report with a gastrointestinal illness earlier in the day. Nic Claxton will likely get the start at center, with Zach Collins filling out the backup minutes down low.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jerami Grant (left calf strain) will not play on Saturday against the Timberwolves.
body: He left Thursday’s game after five minutes and didn’t return. Olivier Maxence-Prosper and Taylor Hendricks were the beneficiaries of that injury. Hendricks could be used as a streamer in twelve team leagues and Maxence-Prosper is a deeper league guy.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Javon Small (personal) has been ruled out against the Timberwolves on Saturday.
body: Small has been an important reserve for Memphis this season, especially as of late. With Ty Jerome expected to return from a four-game absence, Small’s minutes will go to Cam Spencer, who filled in nicely as a starter with Jerome out.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Brandon Ingram (Achilles) is expected to make his season debut against the Rockets on Monday.
body: Ingram has been traveling with the team recently with signs pointing towards an imminent debut. Now Charania has reported that will come Monday against the Rockets. The 29-year-old forward’s return from a partially torn Achilles also coincides with a four-game week for the Clippers.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Ron Holland (knee) is doubtful for Friday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Holland is unlikely to suit up Friday as he’s listed as doubtful with a left knee contusion. The 21-year-old forward was present at shootaround Friday, which is a good sign that the injury isn’t overly serious. Holland’s likely absence Friday won’t impact fantasy basketball.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jalen Smith (illness) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Wizards.
body: Smith popped up on the injury report Friday as questionable with an illness. He’s potentially on the wrong side of questionable given that he only has a few hours to recover before the game. If the 26-year-old forward is ruled out, Nic Claxton could move into the starting lineup.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Stephon Castle had 21 points (7-of-12 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, 12 assists, four steals and two three-pointers against the Clippers on Thursday.
body: Castle bounced back nicely after scoring only 10 points against the Pistons on Tuesday. He has now recorded at least 20 points in three of his last four games. The 22-year-old guard has also posted at least six assists in four consecutive games and at least four steals in two of his last three games. The Spurs have one game remaining this week, against the Pelicans at home Saturday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Julian Champagnie had 20 points (8-of-14 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, one assist and four three-pointers against the Clippers on Thursday.
body: Champagnie moved into the starting lineup Thursday and will likely remain there with Dylan Harper (hip) set to be sidelined for weeks. The 25-year-old forward scored 20 points and made four three-pointers in 29 minutes. He’ll be especially useful to fantasy managers in need of three-point shooting while Harper is out.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Victor Wembanyama had 32 points (13-of-26 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, three assists, one block, one steal and two three-pointers in the Spurs’ 124-112 victory over the Clippers on Thursday.
body: Wembanyama had another excellent game, though he continues to struggle from behind the three-point line. The 22-year-old center is just 3-of-15 from behind the arc over his last two games. Still one of the best players in all of fantasy basketball, Wembanyama’s next chance to break out of his shooting slump will come Saturday against the Pelicans at home.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Charles Bassey had 16 points (6-of-7 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), 13 rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocks against the Grizzlies on Thursday.
body: Bassey was a bright spot for the Warriors on Thursday. The 26-year-old forward led the team with 16 points and had a double-double with 13 rebounds. Bassey was still able to put up a solid fantasy stat line in just 24 minutes. He’s worthy of streaming consideration when he’s in the starting lineup.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Cedric Coward had 19 points (7-of-14 FGs), four rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers against the Warriors on Thursday.
body: Coward is a steady player who contributes fantasy production across the board. The 23-year-old guard once again posted a complete stat line against the Warriors Thursday. Coward should remain in fantasy lineups heading into Saturday’s game against the Timberwolves on the road.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jaylen Wells had 22 points (8-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds and four three-pointers in the Grizzlies’ 126-98 victory over the Warriors on Thursday.
body: Wells had a nice game Thursday against the Warriors with 22 points and seven rebounds. The 23-year-old forward got hot from downtown, sinking four three-pointers. Unfortunately, Wells doesn’t offer much outside of points and threes and is tough to roster in most fantasy basketball formats.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Nate Ament had 18 points (6-of-11 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds and two three-pointers against the Trail Blazers on Thursday.
body: Ament moved into the starting lineup Thursday and the 19-year-old forward had a great game. Ament played 35 minutes and had 18 points and nine rebounds. He proved he’s worth streaming consideration when given the opportunity to start.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jrue Holiday had 22 points (8-of-14 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, seven assists, four steals and two three-pointers against the Bucks on Thursday.
body: Holiday has now recorded at least 21 points, at least six assists and at least three combined steals and blocks in back-to-back games. He stepped up with 22 points on 14 attempts with Deni Avdija (foot) out Thursday. Holiday will continue to see a boost in fantasy value if Avdija remains out.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Scoot Henderson had 27 points (8-of-12 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, one block, one steal and five three-pointers against the Bucks on Thursday.
body: Henderson stepped up with Deni Avdija (foot) out of the lineup Thursday. The 22-year-old guard came out of nowhere to drop 27 points off the bench, which helped lead to a 124-114 victory over the Bucks. Henderson has to be more consistent to merit fantasy consideration, but, for one night, he certainly had an outstanding game.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Damian Lillard had 33 points (10-of-18 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), six rebounds and five three-pointers in the Trail Blazers’ 124-114 victory over the Bucks on Thursday.
body: In Lillard’s first game against the Bucks in Milwaukee since he was waived by the organization two summers ago, the 36-year-old guard predictably lit them up. Lillard torched the Bucks’ defense for 33 points on 18 attempts, connecting on five three-pointers in the process. The Trail Blazers have one game remaining this week against the Knicks on the road Saturday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jonathan Kuminga had 23 points (7-of-13 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, three blocks and two three-pointers against the Knicks on Thursday.
body: Kuminga returned to the floor after a one-game absence due to a shoulder injury. The 24-year-old forward had 23 points, which led the Timberwolves in the loss to the Knicks Thursday. Kuminga will look to build on this performance as his production has been inconsistent at best despite increased opportunities with Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined. His next opportunity will come against the Grizzlies at home on Saturday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jalen Brunson had 21 points (8-of-20 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, seven assists, two steals and four three-pointers against the Timberwolves on Thursday.
body: Brunson has now posted four three-pointers and at least seven assists in three of his last four games. The 30-year-old guard wasn’t very efficient with 21 points on 20 attempts, but he also recorded seven assists and only one turnover. Brunson and the Knicks begin a home back-to-back against the Trail Blazers and Pacers on Saturday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Karl-Anthony Towns had 22 points (9-of-20 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, four assists, three blocks and two three-pointers in the Knicks’ 102-99 victory over the Timberwolves on Thursday.
body: Towns has now recorded at least 21 points in six of his last seven games. The 31-year-old center also leads the league in rebounds per game with 13.9. In the midst of contract turmoil, Towns is having one of his best seasons, which is great news for fantasy managers.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jerami Grant (calf) won’t return to Thursday’s game against the Warriors.
body: After making a three-pointer early in the second quarter, Grant limped back to the locker room before being ruled out with a left calf injury. He finished with three points in five minutes.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: De’Andre Hunter (hip) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Lakers.
body: Hunter returned to the starting lineup Wednesday after a one-game absence due to a hip injury. He’s on the injury report for Friday as questionable with the same hip injury. Dylan Cardwell could move into the starting lineup if Hunter is out again.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Austin Reaves (heel) is out for Friday’s game against the Kings.
body: No surprise here as there’s still no timetable for Reaves to return from a heel injury. Friday will be his fourth missed game in a row. Quentin Grimes should continue to start in his absence.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: The Bucks will start Brayden Burries, Tyler Herro, Nate Amnet, Larry Nance and Kel’el Ware against the Trail Blazers on Thursday.
body: The Bucks have a fresh frontline with Amnet, Nance and Ware all getting the starting nod Thursday. Ware is the most interesting option for fantasy as he should see a significant increase in usage with Myles Turner (shoulder) sidelined.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: The Clippers will start Darius Garland, Max Strus, Derrick Jones Jr., Rui Hachimura and Brook Lopez against the Spurs on Thursday.
body: Los Angeles is changing things up tonight with Strus starting in place of Kris Dunn, who will come off the bench. Neither have been viable in fantasy basketball leagues this season, but we’ll see how this goes.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: The Spurs will start De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell, Julian Champagnie and Victor Wembanyama against the Clippers on Thursday.
body: No surprise here as with Dylan Harper (hip) sidelined for weeks, the Spurs have moved Champagnie into the starting lineup. The 25-year-old forward can be useful to fantasy managers, especially those in need of three-point shooting.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Warriors will start De’Anthony Melton, Brandin Podziemski, Gui Santos, Yaxel Lendeborg and Charles Bassey against the Grizzlies on Thursday.
body: Even with LJ Cryer (back) available, Melton will start for the Warriors. The only other change in the starting lineup for Golden State is Santos subbing in for Draymond Green.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: The Grizzlies will start Cam Spencer, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cam Boozer and Taylor Hendricks against the Warriors on Thursday.
body: With Zach Edey (ankle) out of the lineup, Hendricks will start in his absence. Isaiah Stewart (illness) is also available and figures to play a significant role off the bench.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jonathan Kuminga (shoulder) is available for Thursday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Kuminga is set to return after missing Tuesday’s game against the Trail Blazers with a right shoulder contusion. Cody Williams will move back to the bench with Kuminga in the starting lineup Thursday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Toumani Camara (soreness) is available for Thursday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Camara is available after being listed as questionable with soreness. The 26-year-old forward is in the middle of an iron man streak with Thursday marking his 101st consecutive regular season game.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Deni Avdija (foot) is out for Thursday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Avdija is set to miss his second game in a row with a foot injury. Jayson Kent figures to start again while Jrue Holiday stands to gain the most fantasy value in Avdija’s absence.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Peyton Watson (back) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Pacers.
body: Watson has missed two of the last three games with a lower back issue. His questionable status at least gives him a chance of suiting up Friday against the Pacers. If Watson is out, Sam Merrill could take on a larger role.
author: Nick Shlain
